name: Just Economics
mission: Our mission is to educate, advocate and organize for a more just and sustainable local economy that works for all in Western North Carolina.
activity_or_mission: Our mission is to educate, advocate and organize for a more just and sustainable local economy that works for all in Western North Carolina.
programs:
1. [4a] - Launched a new Living Wage Champions Campaign in Henderson County. - Successfully advocated for higher wages for the lowest paid workers and firefighters at the City of Asheville. - Graduated a virtual class of Voices for Economic Justice and worked with another group of participants in the Fall! - Facilitated 8 Poverty Simulations. - Certified 35 employers new to the Living Wage Certification program in Buncombe County and 5 new employers in Transylvania County. Saw a $1.4 million impact with wage raises given to meet our living wage standards during certification and recertification. - Hosted employer networking events and led the national Living Wage Network. - Co-led the newly formed Buncombe Affordable Housing Network. (expenses $290,312)
2. [4b] - Engaged in the City of Ashevilles Affordable Housing Plan. - Hosted Affordable Housing Advocacy 101 workshops. - Joined the NC Tenants Union. - Co-facilitating Tenants Rights Workshops with Pisgah Legal. - Hosted a Spring Transit Riders Assembly. - Led Asheville Regional Transit Coalitions work to advocate for increased frequency to South Asheville and gain better understanding of microtransit. - Completed a study with partners at UNCA/UNC Gillings on Hospitality Worker Health and Wellbeing - Advocated Transylvania County for Living Wages and a Paid Family Leave policy through public comment, meetings, and an op-ed.
3. [4c] In the aftermath of Hurricane Helene, we: - Delivered supplies to individuals and helped to prevent evictions. - Ramped up our housing work by advocating for zero rent in public housing during the disaster, canvassing in public housing, leading the WNC Tenants Network, hosting a fair housing training, and providing information and support to tenants in both public and private housing. - Supported local businesses advocating for small business grants and providing new ways for individuals to show support for Living Wage Certified employers from near and far. - Organized a disaster relief laundry service organizing 20+ washers in Transylvania County to help do laundry for individuals in Buncombe County without usable water. - Partnered with Swannanoa Communities Together by providing direct staff capacity for a resource center.

name: Charlotte Housing Justice Coalition
mission: The Charlotte Housing Justice Coalition's primary purpose is to advocate for all residents across Mecklenburg County to have quality, affordable housing, helping residents access legal resources, and advocating for residents facing displacement.
programs:
1. Helped maintain housing for a family of five who were facing eviction due to adults in the family's inability to work due to injury and forcing them to be behind on rent. We provided legal resources to this family and helped settle a legal claim with the apartment owner while adults were able to stay housed. Family is currently enjoying stable housing without threat of eviction. (expenses $1,500)
2. Provided legal resources to three students at UNCC facing eviction and discipline from the college due to exercising their First Amendment Right over community concerns about issues of displacement. One of the students was able to maintain their housing while two were able to maintain their path to graduation. (expenses $3,600)
3. Community canvass and community meetings of 182 households near Charlotte-Douglas International Airport (CLT) related to a rezoning and the destruction of historic structures near the airport. Advocated for communities at City Council meetings and Historic Landmark Commission meetings to maintain integrity of potentially historic neighborhoods near the airport that were created in the post-World War II era. A rezoning was withdrawn by CLT due to our advocacy efforts with the community in 2025 as a result of our efforts in 2024. We are now actively working with the communities to explore options to designate neighborhoods as historic as well as explore environmental concerns caused by the airport. (expenses $30,772)
